issues.title: [Bug]: module init returning a proper subtype of error? (e.g. DErr?, error<D>?) is rejected
issues.output: error[SEMANTIC_ERROR]: 'init' function must have return type '()' or  'error?' --> 1725.bal:5:1 (same for `returns error<D>?`)
issues.edge_case_reason: Module init with a distinct-error or parameterised-error optional return type is a rarely used construct.
issues.reasoning: Reproduces on main. Spec (module init): return type must be a subtype of error? and contain (); DErr? and error<D>? qualify, so the check is over-strict. Rejected before BIR → frontend. Related #1710 (class init rules), not a duplicate.

issues.title: [Bug]: XML children step `x/<p:e|f>` fails to parse when the first alternative is a prefixed name
issues.edge_case_reason: XML children step with a namespace-prefixed name as first of several alternatives is rarely used.
issues.reasoning: Reproduces. §6.36 xml-name-pattern allows `p:e|f`; parser rejects a valid program → frontend. No duplicate found.

issues.title: [Bug]: attribute map of a read-only xml:Element is not read-only (`is readonly` is false)
issues.reasoning: Reproduces. §5.3.2: attributes mapping of a read-only xml:Element must have its read-only bit on; lang.xml getAttributes returns that mapping. Concerns lang.xml getAttributes behaviour → langlib (BIR builds the attr map as plain `newMap {| string... |}`, so the fix may touch how the element's attribute map is constructed). Related #1698 (opposite problem).

issues.title: [Bug]: object type descriptor accepts a method-decl named `init`
issues.edge_case_reason: Declaring `init` in an object type descriptor is an unusual (invalid) construct.
issues.reasoning: Reproduces. Spec object types: method-name in a method-decl must not be init; missing compile error → frontend. Related #1252 (init treated as part of shape), not a duplicate.

issues.title: [Bug]: fields included via object-type inclusion (`*T`) are not checked for initialization
issues.output: compiles; runtime: error: unsupported type combination: <nil> + int64 at main(1729.bal:13)
issues.edge_case_reason: Object-type inclusion in a class is ordinary code.
issues.reasoning: Reproduces. Fields from `*A` with no initializer must be definitely assigned by init (§6.8.1); missing compile error lets an int field hold nil. Wrong/missing diagnostic → frontend. Related #1721, #1395.

issues.title: [Bug]: XML template syntax-error columns shift left by 2 per quoted attribute in an earlier XML template
issues.output:
error[SYNTAX_ERROR]: missing double quote token --> 1732.bal:7:21
error[SYNTAX_ERROR]: invalid token --> 1732.bal:7:22 (expected column 23)
issues.edge_case_reason: Needs a syntax error in an XML template after another XML template with quoted attributes.
issues.reasoning: Reproduces. Diagnostic positions drift left by 2 per quoted attribute in an earlier XML template; spec-independent diagnostic quality bug in the parser → frontend.

issues.title: [New Feature]: Add runtime support for configurables
issues.output: fatal[UNIMPLEMENTED_ERROR]: configurable module variables are not supported yet --> main.bal:2:1
issues.reasoning: Feature still missing on main (configurables rejected with UNIMPLEMENTED_ERROR). Runtime-side half of configurable support (value lookup at execution time via PAL); frontend half is #1741. Already a sub-issue of #781. Issue has no Type/* label, so add Type/New Feature.

issues.title: [Bug]: http JSON payloads write an integral float without its fraction
issues.reasoning: Reproduces. ballerina/http json payload serializer drops the fraction of an integral float; lang.value toJsonString gives 10.0, so the float/int distinction is lost on round-trip. Standard library → library, triage-lib.

issues.title: [Bug]: cycle through a function-typed module variable is reported as "expected int, got never"
issues.output: error[SEMANTIC_ERROR]: incompatible type: expected int, got never --> 1750.bal:3:9
issues.edge_case_reason: Initialization cycle through a lambda-valued module variable is an unusual construct.
issues.reasoning: Reproduces. Rejecting is right but the diagnosis is wrong: should be a module-variable cycle error (a → b's body → a). Wrong diagnostic → frontend. Related #1282, #1327, #1483; not a duplicate.

issues.title: [Bug]: inferred typedesc argument is not checked against the parameter's typedesc constraint
issues.output: compiles; runtime: error: function not found: depend at main(1751.bal:6)
issues.edge_case_reason: Dependently-typed external function with a constrained typedesc and an incompatible contextual type.
issues.reasoning: Reproduces. Inferred `<>` typedesc (int[] from context) is not a subtype of the parameter's constraint record {}[]; spec requires a compile error. Missing diagnostic → frontend. Second comment's langlib repro was retracted by its author.

issues.title: [Bug]: compiler panics (nil pointer in semtypes.mappingFormulaIsEmpty) on a recursive record whose field default calls a dependently-typed function
issues.output: panic: runtime error: invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference [signal SIGSEGV] at semtypes.mappingFormulaIsEmpty (semtypes/mapping_ops.go:49)
issues.edge_case_reason: Recursive record whose field default calls a dependently-typed langlib function.
issues.reasoning: Reproduces: Go panic in the front end before any diagnostic → frontend + frontend-crash. Note: spec-check suggests the correct result is a compile error rather than `ok` (inferred t = Leaf, which is not anydata since `next` may hold error), but a crash is wrong either way. Related #1708, #1204, #1295 (different shapes).

issues.title: [Bug]: casting a list constructor to a readonly intersection type panics with "bad type cast"
issues.output: error: bad type cast at main(1753.bal:4); BIR: `%4 = newArray [int, int, never...][%3]{%1, %2}` then `%5 = <readonly&[int...]>(%4)`
issues.edge_case_reason: Casting a list constructor to `T[] & readonly` is ordinary code.
issues.reasoning: Reproduces. Spec type cast: cast type is the contextually expected type of the operand, so the list constructor must build an int[] & readonly value. BIR builds a mutable tuple-typed array ignoring the cast context → BIR wrong → frontend. Related #1148, #1044.

issues.title: [Bug]: http:Client default HTTP_2_0 fails against an HTTP/1.1-only server over http://
issues.output: error: Get "http://127.0.0.1:18766/": http2: frame too large (against python3 -m http.server)
issues.reasoning: Reproduces. ballerina/http default client (HTTP_2_0, http2PriorKnowledge=false) should negotiate h2c via upgrade and fall back to HTTP/1.1 on cleartext; nutcracker uses prior knowledge only. Standard library → library, triage-lib. Related #1586.

notes: All 13 new triage issues reproduce on main. Validity checked from spec by a clean-context subagent (reproducers only): all valid. 1742 is already a sub-issue of #781 (parent labels: frontend, runtime). Possible overlap noticed outside scope: #1478 vs #781 (both 'support configurable module variables').
